name: Can I add a rear addition on a small lot in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: If my lot is narrow or small, is there still enough room for a rear addition without violating lot coverage or open space rules?
mainEntity.text: If my lot is narrow or small, is there still enough room for a rear addition without violating lot coverage or open space rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small lots are often the most difficult candidates for rear-house additions because every square foot matters. Even if there is physical space behind the house, zoning may require a certain amount of open yard, minimum setbacks from side and rear property lines, and limits on how much of the lot can be covered by buildings. In dense Los Angeles neighborhoods, a rear addition can also be constrained by fire access, privacy, drainage, and access to the backyard during construction. A strong concept can still work if the addition is compact, carefully placed, and designed to preserve the required open area. The key is to test the lot against zoning before finalizing the floor plan. Many unsuccessful projects start with a room layout and only later discover the lot cannot support it. A measured site plan and zoning review should come first.
acceptedAnswer.description: Possibly, but small lots often face tighter limits on lot coverage, rear yard open space, side setbacks, and building height. A project can look feasible from the street and still fail because the remaining yard area is too small to meet zoning requirements.
